entries.title: Approvals: review session files and hold them until a release time
entries.summary: With the **Approvals** beta, new session files go through a review workflow before they reach integrations, embeds, galleries, the Public API or the attendee app. Turn it on under **Program → Settings → Files → Require approval for session files**, build multi-step workflows that route files by track, format, file type or uploader, and review from the queue in **Publish → Approvals**. A **release time** can hold files until a date and time or until each session starts, and the **Files** list shows approval status and an **Embargoed** tab.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Approvals; then Program → Settings → Files → Require approval for session files

where.path: Publish → Approvals; Program → Settings → Files; Files list

entries.use_case: Events that must vet slides before they reach the app, website or an integration — or keep them under embargo until the talk — get one review queue and release time instead of email chains and manual uploads.

cs_action.note: Approvals is an Early Access beta that we switch on per event; then the organizer turns on Require approval for session files under Program → Settings → Files.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to stop unapproved slides reaching their app, website or integrations (Swoogo, Bizzabo, ASP), or needs a press or abstract embargo.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with legal, brand or sponsor review of speaker files, or embargoed content, especially ones syncing files to other systems.
internal.gotchas: Files uploaded before approval was turned on are not held for approval, but a release time covers them. A release time holds files even if the workflow or the beta is turned off. A session-start release holds a file until its session has a start time. A step with no reviewers stays pending and is never auto-approved. Un-approving a file stops future syncs but does not remove it from places it already reached.
internal.talk_track: Set up the workflow once and every new slide goes to the right reviewers; nothing leaves Sessionboard until it is approved and its release time has passed, and speakers see where their file stands.

entries.title: History: Attend admin changes in Audit, attendee app activity in a new Attendees tab
entries.summary: Changes your team makes in Attend — the Mobile App editor, check-in, leads, notifications, networking, registration and the rest — now show in **History → Audit**, setting by setting with the old value. A new **Attendees** tab in event and organization **History** lists what attendees did in the app (sign-ins, check-ins, saves, contact swaps, scans and more), with filters, a detail panel per row and CSV export.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

entries.use_case: Organizers can answer "who changed the app?" and "did this attendee check in?" from History, and hand an attendee's activity to support or an accreditor without asking engineering.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks who changed an Attend setting, or needs to check what an attendee did in the app (failed sign-ins, check-ins, scans).
internal.who_should_get_it: Events and organizations on the Attend Mobile App beta.
internal.staff_path: Event → History → Attendees (and org History → Attendees)
internal.gotchas: The Attendees tab appears only where the event has the Attend Mobile App (or, at org level, the org app or an event with it). Rows hold ids and action names, never message text, answers or notes. Activity is kept about 13 months. Pathways-relevant attendee actions (sign-in, check-in, reservations, Q&A, polls, contact swaps and more) also become Signals.
internal.talk_track: Every change to your app is in History with the old value, and the new Attendees tab shows what each attendee did in the app — filter it, open a row, export it.

entries.title: CE quizzes on the session, certificate PDFs, and credit claims in the Attend app
entries.summary: A session's **Credits** panel gets a **Session quiz**: write the quiz on the session itself, set the pass mark and attempts, and optionally require a pass before attendees can claim credit. Publishing the session as a lesson copies the quiz. Attendees can claim credit inside the Attend app, and the certificate page has **Download PDF**.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Credits (with Lessons & Credits for the organization); then Sessions → [session] → Credits → Session quiz

where.path: Sessions → [session] → Credits → Session quiz; Attend app → Credits → claim; certificate page → Download PDF

entries.use_case: CE and CME meetings attach the knowledge check to the session, and attendees take it, claim credit and download their certificate without leaving the app.

cs_action.note: Needs Credits on the event and Lessons & Credits for the organization (both Early Access).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an accredited (CME, CE, CPE) customer asks for post-session quizzes, in-app credit claims or PDF certificates.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations on the Lessons & Credits beta that award credit at events using the Attend Mobile App.
internal.gotchas: Questions lock once anyone has attempted the quiz; the pass mark and attempts can still change. A session quiz takes precedence over a quiz on the lesson made from the session, and a pass on either counts. When a session has no credit in Learning, the app shows its CEU credits as a display-only fallback. The Help Center still describes writing the quiz on the lesson — the article needs updating.
internal.talk_track: Write the quiz on the session, require a pass, and attendees take it, claim credit and download their certificate right in the app.

entries.title: Mobile App editor: body and heading fonts, and a cleaner editor
entries.summary: **Design → Theme** in **Attend → Mobile App** (and the organization app's branding) now has a **Body font** and a **Heading font**, from ten families including Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans, Roboto, Lato, Montserrat, Merriweather and Lora; leaving them empty keeps the phone's system font. The editor also got a tidy-up: one heading per section, **Sign-in & privacy** split into titled sections with a sticky **Save** bar, and **SSO** offered only once your organization has an identity provider.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Mobile App → Design → Theme; org Publish → Mobile App → branding

entries.use_case: The app can use the same typefaces as the event's brand and website, so it looks like the organizer's app rather than a generic one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether the app can match their brand fonts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events and organizations on the Attend Mobile App beta.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Mobile App → Design → Theme
internal.gotchas: Only the ten listed families are available; custom font uploads are not. Fonts are part of the design draft, so attendees see them after Publish, once their app version supports fonts. If SSO is greyed out under Sign-in methods, the organization has no identity provider set up.
internal.talk_track: Pick a body and heading font in Theme and the app takes on your brand's typography.

entries.title: Attend app: sign in with email and registration ID, and Who's Who groups
entries.summary: **Sign-in & privacy** in **Attend → Mobile App** gets a third sign-in method, **Email and registration ID**: attendees enter their email plus an ID from their registration (attendee ID, badge number or confirmation number), with a minimum length and the name attendees see, such as "Member ID". A **Who's Who** section in the editor builds groups of people — board, committees, faculty, staff — from contacts, speakers and registrants, each with an optional role, for a Who's Who page in the app.

enable.path: Attend → Mobile App → Sign-in & privacy → Sign-in methods → Email and registration ID; Attend → Mobile App → Who's Who

where.path: Attend → Mobile App → Sign-in & privacy; Attend → Mobile App → Who's Who; Attend app sign-in screen

entries.use_case: Attendees who cannot get to their email on site sign in with the number on their badge or confirmation, and associations can show their board, committees and faculty in the app.

cs_action.note: Some registration platforms issue short, sequential IDs that are easy to guess. Help the customer pick the confirmation number where they have one, raise the minimum length, and keep Email link and code on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says attendees struggle with the email sign-in link on site, or an association wants its leadership and committees listed in the app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend Mobile App beta whose registration platform syncs IDs to Sessionboard (Cvent, Swapcard, LiveBuzz, Visit and others), and associations with committees or faculty to show.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Mobile App → Sign-in & privacy; Event → Attend → Mobile App → Who's Who
internal.gotchas: Email and ID are always both required, and only live registrants of the event can sign in. Repeated misses lock that email out for 15 minutes. IDs shorter than the minimum never sign anyone in. In Who's Who, people the app will hide (not a public speaker, opted out of the directory, inactive registration, no longer on the event) stay listed with the reason; email and phone are never shown. Groups save one at a time and are not part of the design draft.
internal.talk_track: Attendees can sign in with their email and badge or confirmation number, and you can build Who's Who groups — board, committees, faculty — that show right in the app.

entries.title: Attend app: sponsors, exhibitors and session files
entries.summary: The Attend app now lists the event's sponsors and exhibitors — logo, description, website, tier, linked sessions, and booth numbers from published floor maps — and shows each session's files. Attendees open a file in the app; only files marked **Visible** on the session are offered, never title slides or poster files.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend app → Sponsors / Exhibitors; Attend app → session → files

entries.use_case: Attendees find sponsors, exhibitors and the session handouts in the same app as the agenda, and organizers decide which files they see with the Visible switch they already use.

cs_action.note: Any live registrant can open a session file marked Visible. Ask the customer to check which files are Visible before the app goes live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees get slides or handouts in the app, or wants sponsors and exhibitors listed there.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend Mobile App beta with sponsors, exhibitors or session files.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → [session] → Files (Visible); Event → CRM → Sponsors / Exhibitors
internal.gotchas: A sponsor or exhibitor is listed when the event holds it in that role or a public session links it. Booth numbers come from published floor maps only. A file whose newest version failed the virus scan is skipped, not replaced by an older version. File links expire after 10 minutes and are re-issued when the attendee opens the file again. Needs the Attend app release with partners and files.
internal.talk_track: Sponsors, exhibitors and session handouts are in the app now — you control which files attendees see with the Visible switch.
